newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian government likely to collapse.
newsitem.headline: Estonian government likely to collapse.

text.p: The Baltic state of Estonia faced a political crisis on Thursday as one of the ruling parties was poised to quit the one-year-old coalition government.

The Reform Party, junior partner in the two-party coalition, was to meet later on Thursday whether to leave the coalition in protest over the decision of Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi to sign a cooperation pact with a leading opposition party.
Six Reform Party ministers have already announced their resignation and the Reform Party's board was to meet at six p.m. (1600 GMT) to decide on quitting the coalition.
"I think the probability that we will leave is 99 percent," Reform Party MP Juergen Liigi told Reuters.

Estonia has been plagued by political instability since quitting the former Soviet Union in 1991. The government of Vaehi's Coalition Party and the Reformists is the sixth since independence was regained.
Estonia, the smallest of the three Baltic states, has kept on the path of reform despite political turbulence and is viewed as one of the most successful of the ex-Communist states.
The Reform Party was furious with Vaehi for concluding a cooperation deal with the leading opposition party, the Centre Party, and demanded that he scrap it.
Vaehi refused to comply and tried to persuade his coalition colleagues to stay in the government.
Liigi said most Reform Party MPs believe the Centre and Coalition Parties will link up for a new coalition.

The previous government was a Coalition/Centre party administration but it collapsed amid scandal after the Centre Party leader was found to have taped confidential recordings of conversations with leading politicians.
